title: For affected test selection the deterministic import graph beats cheap models and matches the workhorse
summary: The static import graph finds 98% of truly affected test modules at zero cost and selects 14 of 46 modules on average (about 70% fewer modules than the full suite). Cheap models find only about half of the affected modules, so they are unsafe as selectors. Sonnet trades recall for precision at real cost. Direct consequence: Orchestrator can shorten per-node validation by running import-graph-selected tests first, keeping the full suite as the completion/integration gate (no gate is weakened). A trace-derived map (the label generator itself) is an exact selector at its base commit and a candidate cache.

provenance.author_tier: frontier (Opus 5.5) analysis of deterministic eval output
